entries.summary: inkling added to benchmark — 6/6 OK, avg 85.33, $0.1852 run cost.
details: User asked: 'inkling — is this part of the benchmark? If not add this one as well.'

Pre-flight: searched /tmp/_venice_catalog.json, /tmp/venice_sweep.log, /tmp/venice_re_run2.log, data/results.json, and model_registry.py for 'inkling' — zero hits in benchmark surfaces; confirmed the model EXISTS on Venice (Thinking Machines Lab, 66-layer 975B/41B-active MoE, 1M ctx, $1.25/$5.0625 per M, default reasoning 'high', privacy=private).
Added to model_registry.py (16 models total now).
Fired python3 run_benchmarks.py --run-real --max-tokens 32768 --request-timeout 600 --model inkling. Result: 6/6 ok.
Scores: intent_understanding 52, one_shot_ui 95, brick_breaker 100, pharma_drug_interaction 86, pharma_regulatory_comprehension 85, startup_in_a_weekend 94. Average 85.33.
Cost: $0.185243 (mainstay $9.70 cumulative file_total).

Leaderboard impact: inkling lands at rank 3 by raw avg (behind kimi-k3 89.5 and opus-5 87.67). Among heavy MoE models ($1+ per M range) it has the best score/$ at 460.7 — 4× cheaper than opus-5, 6× cheaper than kimi-k3 per reproducible point.
Only sub-3B-active efficiency models beat it on score/$ (minimax 4018, deepseek 1175, zai-org-glm-5-2 1225) — a different cost-class entirely.
data/results.json now 96 rows; benchmarkviv-standalone.html rebuilt (743,442 bytes, sha c7ca3e45…).

entries.summary: Harness caps raised: 8192 → 32768 tokens, 180s → 600s timeout, with per-run overwrite flags.
details: User identified that 8192-token completion cap + 180-second request timeout were 'artificial ceilings that biased results against slow-thorough models'.
Confirmed: the prior sweep had 5 kimi-k3 calls timing out at 180s and 1 opus-5 call exhausting the 8k cap on brick_breaker_realism.
Patch: MAX_TOKENS=32768, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600.
New CLI flags: --max-tokens N and --request-timeout SEC, for per-run pinning (e.g. apples-to-apples at 8192 for fairness comparisons).
Quirk fixed: harness crashed with `TypeError: str | None` on Python 3.9 — guarded with `from __future__ import annotations` to enable PEP 604 union syntax.

entries.summary: Re-ran 4 failed (model, benchmark) pairs and kimi-k3's 6th call under the new caps.

Concrete wins from the cap-raise: kimi-k3 × brick_breaker went from '180s timeout / 0/100' to '510s, 20,544 tokens, 100/100'.

entries.summary: Survey of Venice /v1/models endpoint — 3 models added in last 7 days.
details: User asked which models were added in the last week. Recency signal is per-row `created` integer epoch timestamp on the catalog; query-string filters (?added_after etc.) are silently ignored by the API.
Window 2026-07-17 → 2026-07-24 UTC returned 3 entries:
· 2026-07-23: claude-opus-5 (Anthropic, 1M ctx, $6/$30 per M) — also claude-opus-5-fast at 2× price; both anonymized.
· 2026-07-20: qwen3-6-35b-a3b (Qwen MoE, ~3B active of 35B), $0.15/$1 per M, private.

Conclusion: Only qwen3-6-35b-a3b was cheap enough to benchmark on the daily $10 cap at scale; opus-5 and opus-5-fast tripped the no-Claude-without-explicit-name rule (lifted by the user's 'Add opus-5' call).
